newsletters.subject: [Learning Drop] Why You’re Still Struggling to Learn Efficiently…
newsletters.summary:
## Learning Drop

### Key Highlights
- The concept of locus of control is crucial for learning efficiency, with an internal locus of control being a powerful predictor of long-term learning success.
- Focusing on things outside of one's ability to control can lead to frustration, stress, hopelessness, and demotivation.
- The idea of internal vs external locus of control is often oversimplified, and there is a hierarchy to the locus of control, with some factors being more stable than others.

### Detailed Points
- The newsletter discusses the concept of locus of control, introduced by psychologist Julian Rotter in the 1950s, which refers to the belief in where control over one's life comes from.
- There are two types of locus of control: internal and external, with internal locus of control meaning that one believes their actions and choices significantly influence their outcomes, and external locus of control meaning that one believes external factors control what happens to them.
- Research shows that a strong internal locus of control is one of the most powerful predictors of long-term learning success, allowing individuals to persist, adapt, and seek help when things aren’t going their way.
- The newsletter highlights that people with an external locus of control often feel helpless in the face of setbacks, blaming outside forces and giving up more easily.
- It also notes that focusing on things outside of one's ability to control can lead to negative emotions and outcomes, and that making excuses is a common behavior when one doesn't feel in control.
- The concept of internal vs external locus of control is often oversimplified, and there is a hierarchy to the locus of control, with some factors being more stable than others, such as ability and effort.
- The newsletter provides examples of unstable factors, such as external events, and stable factors, such as ability, and suggests that individuals should focus on improving their ability and skill to achieve long-term learning success.

## The Rundown AI

### Key Highlights
- The Thinking Machines meltdown: New reports reveal last week’s messy split at Mira Murati’s startup had been brewing behind the scenes, with co-founders unhappy with the company’s direction and OpenAI positioned to scoop up the pieces when things fell apart.
- Google brings on Hume’s CEO and engineers: The company hired Hume AI's CEO and roughly seven engineers as part of a new licensing agreement, marking the latest acqui-hire move by the tech giant.
- Learn any subject with NotebookLM podcasts: A tutorial on how to generate a podcast on any topic using Google’s NotebookLM.
- Runway: 90% can't spot AI-generated videos: Runway published research showing that 90%+ of participants couldn't tell between real footage and image-to-video clips generated by its Gen-4.5 model.

### Detailed Points
- Inside the Thinking Machines meltdown: CTO Barrett Zoph and two other co-founders reportedly confronted Murati just days before his firing, pushing for him to take control of technical decisions. Murati allegedly told Zoph to “just do his job” as CTO and fired him later that week, with nine other TML employees also leaving for OAI or receiving offers.
- Zoph was reportedly speaking to Altman behind Murati’s back for months, with the co-founders unhappy with TML’s direction and pushing for a sale to Meta.
- Zoph will now lead OAI’s enterprise AI sales plans as part of a reorg to help close the gap between research and product teams.
- Google DeepMind hired Hume AI's CEO and roughly seven engineers as part of a new licensing agreement, marking the latest acqui-hire move by the tech giant.
- Hume AI will keep operating under new CEO Andrew Ettinger, continuing to supply voice training data and tools to other labs building conversational AI.
- The deal follows Google's $3B Character AI licensing play last year and mirrors similar moves by Microsoft (Inflection) and Meta (Scale AI's CEO).
- NotebookLM: A system that can be used to make a considerable dent in the firehose of information received each day. It can create audio summaries from newsletters, PDFs, and URLs.
- Runway published research showing that 90%+ of participants couldn't tell between real footage and image-to-video clips generated by its Gen-4.5 model.
- Gen-4.5 currently sits atop Artificial Analysis' text-to-video rankings, with Runway rolling out the new image-to-video features this week.
- Other updates include: OAI CFO Sarah Friar floated "value sharing" at Davos, where the company would take a licensing stake in discoveries made using its AI, starting with drug development; Amazon One Medical launched a new agentic health assistant; xAI released a new update to its Grok Imagine creative suite.

## TLDR Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- TikTok has formed a joint venture to keep its platform operating in the US, with Adam Presser as the CEO of TikTok USDS Joint Venture.
- Kaggle has launched Community Benchmarks, a new way for anyone to build, design, run, and share custom benchmarks for evaluating AI models at no cost.
- Capital One has agreed to buy Brex for $5.15 billion in cash and stock.
- Tesla has launched public Robotaxi rides in Austin with no Safety Monitor.
- Elon Musk expects Tesla to begin selling humanoid robots to the public by the end of 2027.

### Detailed Points
- TikTok's joint venture will operate under defined safeguards to protect national security, with TikTok CEO Shou Chew as a director.
- Kaggle's Community Benchmarks enable users to build evaluations easily, with free access to state-of-the-art AI models, support for multimodal inputs/outputs, and an easy-to-use interface.
- The acquisition of Brex by Capital One is expected to close in the second quarter, with Brex being one of the youngest US startups to join the billion-dollar valuation club.
- Tesla's Robotaxi riders in Austin, Texas, can now hail a Model Y Robotaxi without anyone in the vehicle, although the change has not rolled out to the entire fleet yet.
- Elon Musk warned that initial production for Optimus and the Cybercab will be slow, but eventually will end up being fast.
- GitHub Copilot SDK allows developers to embed the same agentic core that powers GitHub Copilot CLI into any application, providing programmatic access to the production-tested execution loop.
- Epic and Google have a secret $800 million Unreal Engine and services deal, where Epic helps Google market Android, and in return, Google helps market Fortnite.
- Microsoft is using Claude Code internally while selling Copilot, and the company plans to expand its hardware chief's role in the latest sign of CEO candidacy.
- Amazon plans thousands more corporate job cuts next week as part of its broader goal of cutting about 10% of its corporate workforce.

## Staying Ahead with AI

### Key Highlights
- Google's new research experiment, Learn Your Way, transforms static textbooks into personalized, interactive learning materials using AI.
- The tool can convert textbooks into five different formats: immersive text with quizzes, slides with narration, audio lessons, mind maps, and section-level quizzes with adaptive feedback.
- Learn Your Way is powered by LearnLM, Google's pedagogy-focused AI model, and is currently available as a research experiment with 16 live demos.

### Detailed Points
- Learn Your Way takes any PDF textbook and rewrites it based on the user's interests, such as football, music, or food, to make complex topics more engaging and accessible.
- The tool breaks down long chapters into digestible chunks, adds AI-generated illustrations, and includes interactive questions throughout the text.
- The five learning formats generated by Learn Your Way include:
  * Immersive text with embedded quizzes: interactive text with quizzes and feedback.
  * Slides with narration: lecture-style videos with conversational summaries and visual examples.
  * Audio lessons: teacher-student dialogue explaining complex concepts in an engaging way.
  * Mind maps: hierarchical knowledge visualization to help students see the big picture.
  * Section-level quizzes with adaptive feedback: quizzes that adapt to the student's responses and provide instant feedback.
- Learn Your Way runs a two-step transformation: re-leveling the text to the user's grade level and injecting interest-based examples to make the content more relatable and engaging.
- The tool has been tested with 60 students, showing an 11% better recall after 3-5 days, and is expected to reshape how students engage with learning materials if subsequent research confirms its effectiveness.
- Other tools mentioned include ChartGen AI, a web-based, AI-driven chart generator, Dreamlux, an AI-powered video generator, and Accordio, an AI-powered contract, proposal, and invoice builder for freelancers.

newsletters.summary:
## AI Breakfast

### Key Highlights
- OpenAI wants a cut of whatever you build with its AI, introducing a "technology empowerment fee" for commercialization of AI-aided discoveries.
- Google is racing toward emotionally intelligent AI, acquiring Hume AI and launching "Personal Intelligence" in AI Mode.
- Apple is replacing Siri with 'Campos' and building an AirTag-sized AI wearable.

### Detailed Points
- OpenAI is testing a pricing model that would take a cut of whatever you build with its AI, instead of charging purely for API calls. This "technology empowerment fee" would be based on the revenue generated from AI-aided discoveries, such as patents, licensing, or product sales.
- OpenAI's CEO Sam Altman announced that the company added over $1 billion in annual recurring revenue from API customers in the last month alone.
- Google acquired Hume AI's CEO Alan Cowen and top engineers to build voice interfaces that read human emotion, using context-aware speech synthesis and affective recognition.
- Google launched "Personal Intelligence" in AI Mode, which processes prompts in real-time using metadata, not raw data, and is available for U.S. subscribers.
- Apple is rebuilding Siri and prototyping AI devices, including a system-wide chatbot called Campos that replaces Siri in iOS 27 and macOS 27.
- Apple is also building an AirTag-sized AI wearable with dual cameras, three mics, a speaker, and wireless charging.
- OpenAI launched the Stargate Community program, funding its own electricity through solar-plus-storage in Wisconsin, project-financed batteries in Michigan, and dedicated Texas grid buildouts.
- Google DeepMind is hiring a Chief AGI Economist to study how AGI could reshape labor, markets, and finance.
- Various other companies and researchers are working on new AI tools and technologies, including Anthropic, ElevenLabs, and Volvo.

### New AI Tools
- Cursor 2.4 adds parallel Subagents and AI image generation with Nano Banana Pro.
- Niches Hunter is a tool for finding profitable iOS niches.
- Blink Agent Builder is a vibe-coding platform for building AI apps and agents.
- Openwork is an open-source TypeScript framework for building AI apps and agents.
- Fimo is an AI website builder that generates multi-page websites with templates and a built-in CMS.
- Mastra is a desktop UI for DeepAgentsJS that helps build and run agent workflows.

## JournalClub.io Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- A recent paper by Magargal et al. from Lehigh University presents a method for projection-based model-order reduction via graph autoencoders suited for unstructured meshes, combining Petrov-Galerkin methods with graph autoencoders for efficient simulation of complex systems.
- The method addresses the limitations of traditional proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for nonlinear problems and unstructured meshes.
- The graph autoencoder learns a nonlinear compression of high-dimensional data, and the Petrov-Galerkin projection ensures stability and accuracy in the reduced-order model.

### Detailed Points
- The paper discusses the historical background of model-order reduction, starting from Boris Galerkin's work on representing solutions using a finite set of functions and projecting governing equations onto that space.
- The limitations of Galerkin's method for certain problems, such as convection and wave-driven systems, led to the development of Petrov-Galerkin methods, which allow for a separate test space for the residual.
- The authors propose a graph autoencoder that works directly on unstructured meshes, representing the mesh as a graph and using spectral clustering to build a hierarchy of coarser graphs.
- The encoder uses message passing and pooling operations to compress the high-dimensional data into a low-dimensional latent space, and the decoder reconstructs the original data from the latent space.
- The Petrov-Galerkin projection is used to evolve the system stably in the learned low-dimensional space, ensuring that the solution satisfies the original physics equations.
- The method is demonstrated to be efficient and accurate for simulating complex systems, such as fluid flow around an airplane wing or shock wave propagation.
- The paper provides a detailed comparison with traditional methods, such as POD and CNNs, and discusses the advantages of the proposed approach for nonlinear problems and unstructured meshes.

## The Code by Superhuman

### Key Highlights
- The rise of AI subagents and their potential to revolutionize coding and development.
- Introduction of subagents in Cursor 2.4 that can split projects across parallel workers for faster development.
- Anthropic's Claude Code now supports multi-agent tasks that sync automatically.
- Liquid AI's open-source reasoning model LFM2.5-1.2B-Thinking that can run on a phone.

### Detailed Points
- **AI Subagents**: Big tech companies are investing in AI subagents, which are independent workers that can handle discrete parts of a task in parallel. This technology has the potential to significantly speed up coding and development processes.
- **Cursor 2.4**: The latest release of Cursor introduces subagents that can split projects across parallel workers, improving coding speed and efficiency. Default subagents can tackle codebase research, terminal commands, and parallel work streams automatically.
- **Anthropic's Claude Code**: Claude Code has been upgraded with a new Tasks system, enabling multiple subagents to collaborate on complex projects simultaneously through parallel sessions that automatically sync progress.
- **Liquid AI's LFM2.5-1.2B-Thinking**: This open-source reasoning model can fit in under 900 MB and run fully offline on devices, using internal "thinking traces" to reason through problems before outputting concise answers.
- **Engineering Leadership**: A blog post argues that early-stage startups should avoid managing engineers, as it wastes energy and hiring inherently motivated people is more effective.
- **Staff Engineer Role**: A comprehensive guide outlines the 14 skills backend engineers need to reach Staff level, including strategic context management, modular codebases, and investing in reusable workflows.
- **Palantir's AI Agents**: Palantir has released a technical deep-dive on the security dimensions of AI agents, emphasizing the importance of observability and granular tool access policies.

## Mindstream

### Key Highlights
- Apple is replacing Siri with a full AI chatbot, called Campos, later this year, which will support real conversational back-and-forth and will be integrated across iPhone, iPad, and Mac.
- Australia's National Reconstruction Fund has invested $20 million in neuroscience startup Omniscient Neurotechnology to develop AI-powered brain mapping technology.
- Amazon CEO Andy Jassy says tariffs are now pushing prices up on Amazon as sellers run out of pre-tariff inventory and pass higher costs to consumers.

### Detailed Points
- Apple's new chatbot, Campos, will be unveiled in June at Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference and released in September as part of iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27.
- The chatbot will allow users to search the web, generate content and images, summarize information, analyze files, and control device features.
- Apple's chatbot will use an Apple-designed interface but rely heavily on AI models developed by Google, with Apple paying Google roughly $1 billion a year for access.
- Omniscient Neurotechnology's platform, Quicktome, uses AI to map the brain's individual network of connections and is already approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
- The funding will support the commercial rollout of Quicktome, expansion of the company's data science team, and development of new clinical applications.
- The Cure's 1979 classic "Boys Don't Cry" has surpassed one billion streams on Spotify.
- Gordon Ramsay has warned that UK tax and business rate changes are pushing hospitality toward a "bloodbath".
- Suni Williams has retired from NASA after 27 years, ending a record-setting career.

- A webinar is scheduled for January 23rd at 1PM PST / 4PM EST to discuss an alternative to Zillow's Premier Agent service for real estate agents.
- The webinar will cover how intent data can help identify motivated sellers and buyers, and how Real Intent's solution is up to 90% more affordable than Zillow's Premier Agent.
- Real Intent is currently only working with 1 broker or agent per zip code.

### Detailed Points
- The webinar will explain how intent data helps identify motivated sellers and buyers at the optimal time, and provide real-world examples of agents successfully leveraging intent data in their businesses.
- Agents who have used Real Intent have seen significant results, including one agent who increased seller meetings 2-fold and listed 2 properties in the first month, and another who got a listing in their free trial week.
- Real Intent's solution is exclusive, with all zip codes being exclusive to one agent or broker, and some brokers have even secured entire counties.
- The webinar will also cover how agents can use intent data to get a competitive edge in their market, and how Real Intent's technology can help them achieve this.
- The expected runtime of the webinar is approximately 30 minutes.
